To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RBF classifiers are equivalent to a special kind of statistical model, that this model is a mixture model, and that this model is easily learned from the RBF.

(1) RBF classifiers are mixture-of-experts classifiers; (2) RBF classifiers can be designed by optimizing a statistical criterion; (3) unlabeled data can be used to enhance the design of the RBF classifier; and (4) new data to classify can be incorporated into the RBF classifier design, thereby enhancing the classification performance of the RBF.

RBF classifiers are equivalent in form to Bayes-optimal classifiers for a mixture model, that the relevant mixture model is easily determined given any RBF, and that the mixture-based interpretation leads naturally to a statistical learning objective and to a combined learning and using paradigm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of RBF classifiers, the statistical interpretation of their decision functions, a learning objective, and the use of unlabeled data in learning.
the design of RBF classifiers and the statistical interpretation of their decision function.
the design of RBF classifiers and with the learning of the parameters of a new type of mixture model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RBF classifier is a special kind of a mixture model.

the RBF classifier is equivalent to the Bayes optimal discriminant of a special mixture model and that a combined learning and using procedure is a natural way to use this equivalence to improve classification.
the RBF classifier, in its standard form, is a special case of a mixture model classifier, and that the standard form is not the best possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RBF classifier, which is widely used in practice, can be interpreted as a special mixture model, which can be learned and used in a combined learning and classification paradigm.
we show that RBF classifiers are mixture models, and we suggest a statistical learning objective for designing them.
we provide a new interpretation of the RBF classifier, a new objective to design RBFs, and a new paradigm for combining learning and use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RBF model, as well as other models with a similar form, is a type of statistical model.
RBF classifiers are not just a heuristic, but rather a special kind of statistical model that can be learned and used in a principled way.
RBF classifiers are a form of mixture models and that this fact can be exploited to improve their performance.
